summary: This note describes the flow characteristics of Niagara Falls on the Niagara River, which drains Lake Erie into Lake Ontario. It covers peak and average flow rates over Horseshoe Falls, how water is diverted to hydroelectric facilities under the 1950 Niagara Treaty, and the falls' location between Buffalo and Toronto. The main point is that the combined falls have the highest flow rate of any waterfall with a vertical drop over 165 feet, and Horseshoe Falls is the most powerful in North America by flow.
one_line: Overview of Niagara Falls' water flow rates, seasonal variation, hydroelectric diversion under the 1950 Niagara Treaty, and location on the Niagara River.
key_facts: The peak flow over Horseshoe Falls was recorded at 225,000 cubic feet (6,400 m) per second.
The average annual flow rate over Horseshoe Falls is 85,000 cubic feet (2,400 m) per second.
Because flow is a direct function of the Lake Erie water elevation, Niagara Falls typically peaks in late spring or early summer.
During the summer months, at least 100,000 cubic feet (2,800 m) per second of water traverses the falls.
About 90% of the summer flow goes over Horseshoe Falls, while the balance is diverted to hydroelectric facilities.
A weir called the International Control Dam, with movable gates upstream from Horseshoe Falls, is used to divert water.
The falls' flow is further halved at night.
During the low tourist season in winter, the flow remains a minimum of 50,000 cubic feet (1,400 m) per second.
Water diversion is regulated by the 1950 Niagara Treaty and administered by the International Niagara Board of Control (IJC).
The Niagara River drains Lake Erie into Lake Ontario.
The combined falls have the highest flow rate of any waterfall in the world with a vertical drop of more than 165 feet (50 m).
Horseshoe Falls is the most powerful waterfall in North America, as measured by flow rate.
Niagara Falls is 17 miles (27 km) north-northwest of Buffalo, New York.
Niagara Falls is 75 miles (121 km) south-southeast of Toronto.
The falls lie between the twin cities of Niagara Falls, Ontario, and Niagara Falls, New York.
